prompt: In right triangle $ABC$ with the right angle at $C$, which ratio equals $\sin A$?
hint: Say the whole mnemonic out loud: SOH-CAH-TOA.

hints.text: Say the whole mnemonic out loud: SOH-CAH-TOA.
SOH is the first piece: Sine = Opposite / Hypotenuse.

explanation: SOH-CAH-TOA packs all three ratios into one word.
SOH says Sine is Opposite over Hypotenuse, CAH says Cosine is Adjacent over Hypotenuse, and TOA says Tangent is Opposite over Adjacent.
So $\sin A$ is the opposite side divided by the hypotenuse.

alternativeExplanations.title: Spot the imposters
steps: Adjacent over hypotenuse is cosine, and opposite over adjacent is tangent — both real ratios, just not sine.
Hypotenuse over opposite is sine turned upside down, which would give answers bigger than 1 and cannot be sine.
